MS-S.src: Counts and % of expected vote: AP, as carried on Fox News' Mississippi results page ('Source: The Associated Press', last updated 7:57 a.m. ET Friday); vote totals unchanged from the 9:51 p.m. Thursday reading
MS-S.note: Too close to call: Colom leads by 1,813 votes (466,775 to 464,962) in AP's count as of 7:57 a.m. ET Friday (via Fox News' AP-credited results page, 95.65% of expected vote; vote totals unchanged since 6:51 p.m. ET Thursday; Yahoo News reports the same 1,813-vote margin from AP as of 6 a.m. ET Friday), up from 1,724 at midday Thursday and 1,138 Wednesday evening; between the 3:41 p.m. and 6:51 p.m. readings the count added 549 votes for Colom, 460 for Hyde-Smith and 29 for Pinkins. The lead was 65 at 11:30 a.m. CT Wednesday, 43 at 3 a.m. and 28 overnight. Outstanding: about 3,600 absentee-by-mail ballots (Secretary of State Michael Watson, Nov. 4) and an unknown number of affidavit ballots, for which no official count exists (AP: several thousand, and 'decisive'; Colom campaign: 10,000 to 15,000; state Republican Party chairman Mike Hurst: about 17,000; Magnolia Tribune cites unconfirmed reports of upwards of 18,000), which counties are verifying now; Harrison County will not count affidavit ballots until Nov. 10 and DeSoto County no earlier than that day (Queen City Newsfeed, Nov. 5). The National Republican Senatorial Committee has asked election officials to segregate provisional ballots (Election Law Blog, Nov. 5); the Colom campaign says segregation would violate voter privacy and is not allowed under the state elections code (Election Law Blog headline, Nov. 5). Affidavit voters have until Nov. 10 to show ID; mail ballots postmarked by Election Day can arrive through Nov. 10; counties certify by Nov. 13, and the Secretary of State's office expects it may take until then for the race to be called (WLBT). Colom said Wednesday his campaign is 'prepared to litigate'; Hyde-Smith said Thursday that she remains confident and that officials are continuing the normal process of counting outstanding ballots; the NAACP says it has sent legal, policy and field staff to the state (Yahoo News, Nov. 6). No runoff in a federal general election (plurality wins); Mississippi has no automatic recount, and a recount would need a court order (AP). AP has not called the race.

KS-G.src: Counts and % of expected vote: AP, as carried on Fox News' Kansas results page ('Source: The Associated Press', last updated 7:52 a.m. ET Friday); vote totals unchanged from the 9:56 p.m. Thursday reading

Mail ballots postmarked by Election Day are accepted through Friday Nov. 6; provisional ballots are reviewed at county canvasses (6 to 13 days after the election). Secretary of State Scott Schwab ordered a close-race audit of 10% of precincts in each county because election-night margins were within 1% (KSHB). Holscher declared victory Wednesday; Masterson said the margin is narrow enough that Kansas law calls for another look and could request a recount after county certification (state-paid if within 0.5%; KCUR / Kansas Reflector). AP has not called the race.
